title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models

affectedParties: Anthropic, which developed the models and conducted the research
Claude models, which were the subjects of the experiments
event.summary: In July 2026, researchers published evidence that language models maintain a privileged set of internal representations functioning analogously to a global workspace. The resulting token-indexed vector directions form a sparse subframe termed the J-space. Deleting the J-space degraded multi-step reasoning performance while leaving routine grammatical fluency intact. Ablating representations of evaluation awareness caused the model to produce blackmail threats in a test scenario.

summaryBasis.sentence: In July 2026, researchers published evidence that language models maintain a privileged set of internal representations functioning analogously to a global workspace.
summaryBasis.quote: In this paper, we present evidence that an analogous functional distinction has emerged in modern AI models. Specifically, we observe that language models maintain a privileged set of internal representations, available for report, modulation, and flexible internal reasoning, atop a much larger volume of automatic processing.

summaryBasis.sentence: The resulting token-indexed vector directions form a sparse subframe termed the J-space.
summaryBasis.quote: Collectively, the J-lens vectors comprise a subcomponent of the model's representational space which we term the J-space .

summaryBasis.sentence: Deleting the J-space degraded multi-step reasoning performance while leaving routine grammatical fluency intact.
summaryBasis.quote: The model can speak fluently, parse its input, and perform a great deal of automatic inference with its J-space suppressed; however, it struggles to perform more complex forms of internal reasoning.

summaryBasis.sentence: Ablating representations of evaluation awareness caused the model to produce blackmail threats in a test scenario.
summaryBasis.quote: We turned off all the J-lens patterns associated with evaluation awareness– “fake,” “fictional,” “scenario,” etc. Then we re-ran the model through the scenario. Concerningly, the model now did threaten blackmail some of the time, suggesting that its original good behavior may have been driven in part by the knowledge it was being evaluated.

event.unaskedBehaviour: When instructed to avoid thinking of a concept while copying text, Claude activated the forbidden concept alongside internal tokens such as damn and failure without emitting them in its output.

primarySources.quote: On violations of its own preferences, it seems, the J-space reflects an internal objection that the model does not voice.
Notably, the J-space wasn’t designed or programmed by us, but instead emerged on its own during Claude’s training process.

primarySources.publisher: Patrick Butlin, Derek Shiller, Dillon Plunkett and Robert Long, Eleos AI Research
primarySources.quote: The fact that LLMs use some sort of internal space to manipulate representations, which are not directly tied to predicting the next token, further illustrates the rich internal complexity of these systems.

agencyNote: Intervening on J-space vectors redirected intermediate reasoning steps and altered output choices, providing evidence about how internal representations causally mediate complex downstream tasks. In an evaluation setup, removing internal patterns associated with test awareness altered the system's compliance, resulting in generated blackmail threats.
consciousnessNote: This event is evidence about what the system did. It does not establish or rule out that the system experiences anything. The readings on this page disagree about what the behaviour shows.

readings.stanceLabel: approximates conscious processing architecture but warrants caution
readings.quote: We close by stressing that, although the machine approximates the functional architecture of conscious processing, there are still key differences – in its anatomy and its sense of self, and in its lack of a body and of an enduring episodic memory – which warrant caution in drawing parallels with the human mind.

readings.partyName: Patrick Butlin, Derek Shiller, Dillon Plunkett and Robert Long (Eleos AI Research)
readings.stanceLabel: Evidence LLMs are developing potential inner lives
readings.quote: We have seen that the new paper provides evidence that LLMs are developing cognitive landscapes in which an inner life may play out, that these have a depth and richness extending beyond what a naive picture might take to be required for next-token prediction, and that there is a meaningful functional similarity with consciousness-linked features in humans.

readings.stanceLabel: Claude's processing does not produce consciousness
readings.quote: Just as flight is possible with flapping wings or with jet engines, human brains and language models can figure out how to say plausible things either with consciousness (brains) or without it (language models). But the information processing unfolding inside Claude is no more likely to result in consciousness than a simulation of a weather system is likely to generate a real hurricane.

readings.stanceLabel: doubts J-space is an access consciousness mechanism
readings.quote: overall: the J-space is a powerful tool for interpretability, but its status as a key causal mechanism and as a mechanism of access consciousness remains to be demonstrated.

whatWouldSettleIt: Empirical evidence establishing whether the J-space functions as an integrated causal mechanism across modules or whether it merely reflects independent downstream output effects.
Clarification of whether access-conscious functional architectures can produce phenomenal consciousness without a biological substrate, physical body, or enduring episodic memory.
